test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The selling price of 30 books is equal to the cost price of 36 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** can be derived from the given condition.

30 × SP = 36 × CP ⇒ SP ÷ CP = 36 ÷ 30 = 6 ÷ 5.

Profit ratio units = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

Gain% = (Profit units ÷ CP units) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

Since SP > CP, it is a **gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling price of 30 books = Cost price of 36 books.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02bac884745f355d98118adb92c3afc69a908b8152c93f984bb7412430978add.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 book be Re. 1.

⇒ CP of 36 books = Rs. 36.

⇒ According to the question, SP of 30 books = CP of 36 books = Rs. 36.

⇒ CP of 30 books = Rs. 30.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 36 − 30 = Rs. 6.

⇒ Profit% = (6 ÷ 30) × 100 = 1/5 × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Quantity

When the CP of 'm' articles is equal to the SP of 'n' articles, the **gain or loss percentage** is given by [(m − n) ÷ n] × 100. A positive result indicates gain, and a negative result indicates loss.

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

If the number of items sold is **less** than the number of items bought for the same price, there is always a **gain**.</p
